mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last three weekly observations (-22.7, -44.1, -46.1, -50.1). This monotonic negative momentum reflects an unresolved suppression of retail activity that will persist by inertia, pushing the next four-week mean further below the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28 days despite four consecutive weeks of decline, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES exceeding 10 percentage points (as seen from t-1w to t-0w: -43.4 to -56.3) signals active tightening of mobility restrictions. Such policy tightening mechanically suppresses non-essential retail visits over the following two weeks, pulling RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -43.4 to -56.3 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks despite a greater than 10-point weekly drop in WORKPLACES, the policy-tightening trigger is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has risen each week (10.3, 18.9, 21.3, 24.3) while TRANSIT has fallen sharply (-41.3 to -73.6). This joint pattern indicates entrenching stay-at-home behavior: reduced transit use combined with rising residential presence compounds to suppress discretionary retail trips over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose and TRANSIT fell concurrently across all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL continues rising and TRANSIT continues falling, the compounding stay-at-home mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stage 4 style lockdown regime, a weekly PARKS decline exceeding 20 points (as from t-2w -32.6 to t-1w -53.1) indicates outdoor movement restrictions are actively enforced, which in turn curtails incidental retail stops near parks and public spaces within the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -32.6 to -53.1 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a PARKS drop greater than 20 points, the park-restriction linkage is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The observed weekly cadence of declining RETAIL_REC values mirrors a recurring short-cycle seasonal pattern typical of early lockdown phases, where each successive week deepens the prior week's drop before plateauing. This seasonal extrapolation predicts continued, though decelerating, decline over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:weekly RETAIL_REC declines have been decelerating in magnitude (-21.4, -2.0, -4.0 point changes)
failure_condition: If the week-on-week RETAIL_REC decline reverses sign or accelerates beyond historical deceleration pattern, the seasonal extrapolation hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has fallen steadily from 8.0 to -22.1, suggesting initial panic-buying behavior has subsided and essential-shopping frequency is normalizing. Once GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20, this signals behavioral stabilization that typically precedes a short-term rebound in adjacent RETAIL_REC visits as households resume blended errand trips.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues declining in the week after GROCERY_PHARM crosses below -20, the stabilization-rebound hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both falling sharply and concurrently (WORKPLACES -13.9 to -56.3; TRANSIT -41.3 to -73.6). Their joint collapse compounds reduced commuter-linked retail activity, since fewer people are both working away from home and using transit to reach retail precincts, producing a deeper four-week decline in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's four-week mean rises despite continued joint decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the compounding commuter-retail mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a confirmed stage 4 lockdown regime, the simultaneous deep declines across RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES alongside rising RESIDENTIAL indicate that government restrictions are at peak severity. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC is mechanically capped near current depressed levels and will not meaningfully recover until restrictions ease, keeping the next four-week mean at or below the last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:all mobility categories except RESIDENTIAL are deeply negative and still worsening at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean while the stage 4 lockdown regime remains in force, the policy-cap hypothesis is rejected.
